To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pulse arrival times from RRATs are non-random on time-scales of months to years, and that pulse emission from at least some RRATs is not random on hour-long time-scales.
the pulse arrival times of six of the RRATs are found to be periodic, and that the pulse detection rates of all eight are found to be non-random on time-scales of weeks to years.
the pulse arrival times of RRATs exhibit both periodic and non-periodic components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the radio properties of rotating radio transient (RRT) sources from the point of view of time-series analysis of pulse arrival times.
the properties of the radio emission from RRATs, in particular the long-term stability and the randomness of the pulse emission.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RRATs are not random, that they are periodic and that they do not emit doublets and triplets.
RRATs are not a single class of pulsar.
RRATs are a diverse group of pulsars, and that the properties of their pulse arrival times are consistent with a wide range of models for RRATs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RRATs are not simply pulsars with intermittent emission, but rather that they have a more complex time dependence in the emission process.
RRATs are not random emitters on long time-scales and that their emission can be described by a combination of a random Poisson process and a periodic process.
all RRATs exhibit some level of long-term (i.e. years) non-random pulse emission, while the short-term (i.e hours) emission is random.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RRATs are a heterogeneous class of pulsar-like radio emitters.
RRAT emission is random on short time-scales, but not on long time-scales, suggesting that the emission mechanism for RRATs is similar to that of normal pulsars.
RRATs are a very diverse class of objects, with some exhibiting very different properties from others.
